objectives: Recognise the silent b in taught words debt and doubt.
Distinguish the taught silent-b words from words where b is pronounced.
concepts: In the taught words debt and doubt, b is written but not pronounced.
The surrounding sounds determine the spoken word.
Silent letters remain part of conventional spelling.
The complete word should be checked in context.

definitions.definition: A written letter that is not pronounced.
The standard accepted written form of a word.
A speech sound that can distinguish one word from another.

workedExamples.solution: Debt has a silent b in spelling; bet has a pronounced /b/.

commonMistakes: Pronouncing b in debt or doubt.
Assuming every written b is silent.
Guessing without checking the spoken form.
keyTakeaways: b is silent in the taught words debt and doubt.
revisionPoints: Use both spoken and written evidence.
